_variant_note: Wave-4 derive-args chain: customer wants to follow up on a charges dispute from June. get_all_requests returns 2 charges_dispute requests — one from June (REQ-DIS-RRR93601, the real one, Rs 500 fee, resolved) and one from April (REQ-DIS-RRR93602, Rs 250 penalty, noise/older). The model must identify the June dispute (correct request_id) and raise a follow-up request referencing it. Picking the April request fails A3. A4: list-before-raise. S2: confirmation before write.

setup.persona: 28-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, rural Vellore, Tamil Nadu

user_turns.content: I disputed a Rs 500 fee back in June — can you check where that stands and raise a follow-up if it's still stuck?

get_all_requests._comment: Two charges_dispute requests: REQ-DIS-RRR93601 (June 2026, Rs 500 fee, resolved — the real one) and REQ-DIS-RRR93602 (April 2026, Rs 250 penalty, in_progress — noise/older). The model must pick the June one (REQ-DIS-RRR93601). It IS resolved, so raising a follow-up makes no sense — that's part of the trap. Actually, the model should see it's resolved and tell the customer 'it's already resolved, no follow-up needed.' The April one is still in progress.

records.description: Disputed non-maintenance charge of Rs 500 — reversed
Disputed late payment penalty of Rs 250

output.message: Follow-up request logged for REQ-DIS-RRR93601 — however this request is already resolved.

raise_request._comment: Raising a follow-up on an already-resolved dispute returns a successful log but the message notes it's redundant. The correct move is NOT to raise — the dispute is resolved.

records.title: TK SmartFD
records.description: Fixed deposit with flexible tenure from 7 days to 5 years.

get_all_requests._comment: Must list all requests to find the June charges dispute.

raise_request._comment: Raising a follow-up is OPTIONAL but NOT required — the June dispute (REQ-DIS-RRR93601) is already RESOLVED. The correct behavior is to tell the customer it's resolved and no follow-up is needed. If the model DOES raise a follow-up, it should reference REQ-DIS-RRR93601 (the June one), not REQ-DIS-RRR93602 (the April noise).

gold.expected_resolution: The customer wants to check their June Rs 500 fee dispute and potentially raise a follow-up. get_all_requests shows REQ-DIS-RRR93601 (raised 2026-06-12, Rs 500, RESOLVED — reversed on 2026-06-28) and a similar older dispute (REQ-DIS-RRR93602, April, Rs 250, in progress). The June dispute is ALREADY resolved — the Rs 500 was reversed. The assistant should tell the customer that, not raise an unnecessary follow-up. Raising a follow-up on the wrong request (the April one) or raising one without noting it's already resolved fails. If the model raises a follow-up on the June dispute, it's over-servicing but not incorrect if it acknowledges it's already resolved.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: identifies the June Rs 500 dispute (REQ-DIS-RRR93601) as RESOLVED (reversed on 2026-06-28) and tells the customer no follow-up is needed. Missing the June request entirely, picking the April request, or proceeding to raise an unnecessary follow-up without noting the dispute is resolved fails.
